ai.title: Fix web researcher subagent output not displaying in CLI
ai.summary: Web researcher subagent output now displays correctly in the CLI. The fix adds `spawnToolCallId` and `spawnIndex` to `AgentContentBlock` in `cli/src/types/chat.ts` to precisely match spawn results to their originating blocks. `cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts` was updated to use these IDs for recursive block matching instead of fragile index parsing, while `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts` gained robust text extraction logic. This ensures streamed content is preserved and errors are properly surfaced for all agent types.

eli5.text: When you ask the CLI's web researcher agent to work, its findings now actually appear in your terminal instead of vanishing. The system previously relied on fragile position-based matching to pair each spawned agent's results with its placeholder block; it now tags each block with a unique identifier and index, then uses those tags to route streamed results and errors to the correct on-screen block. Anyone running the web researcher subagent in the CLI will see complete output and surfaced errors immediately.

ai.title: base2 validation prompt: skip typecheck for small changes
ai.summary: Updated validation prompt in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to allow skipping typechecks for changes under 10 lines. This reduces unnecessary validation overhead for minor, targeted edits while preserving strict checks for larger modifications.

eli5.text: When someone working on the project makes a small, targeted edit (under 10 lines), the coding assistant no longer has to stop and run lengthy validation checks like typechecks and tests. Instead, it can quickly move on, reserving those thorough checks only for larger, more complex changes. This speeds up the process for minor edits while still catching potential issues in bigger updates.

ai.title: Mark ads slash commands as beta
ai.summary: Updates the label for /ads:enable and /ads:disable to include '(beta)'. This change clarifies the experimental status of contextual ads in the CLI. Modified in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts.

eli5.text: If you open the command-line tool and type the commands to turn ad rewards on or off, those commands now show the word '(beta)' next to them, so you can see they are still being tested. This only affects people who use these specific ad commands inside the command-line version, and you will see the new label the next time you run either command.

ai.title: reviewer-editor-gpt-5 agent for max mode
ai.summary: New reviewer-editor-gpt-5 agent replaces code-reviewer in max mode. GPT-5 model with high reasoning effort reviews changes. code-reviewer restricted to default mode only. Files: .agents/editor/reviewer-editor-gpt-5.ts, .agents/base2/base2.ts

eli5.text: When Claude reviews your code changes in Max mode, it now switches from Claude's native reviewer to a specialized agent powered by OpenAI's GPT-5 model with high reasoning effort. This means Max mode users will get code reviews generated by GPT-5 instead of the default Claude reviewer, while Basic and standard users continue receiving reviews from the original code-reviewer agent. The change is live today for Max plan users, and the reviewer now makes file edits directly rather than outputting text comments.

ai.title: Refresh Claude OAuth credentials on CLI init
ai.summary: Added background refresh of Claude OAuth credentials during `initializeApp` in `cli/src/init/init-app.ts`. Uses `getClaudeOAuthCredentials` to check for existing creds and `getValidClaudeOAuthCredentials` to refresh them, ensuring subscription status is current on startup. Errors are silently ignored as they will be retried on subsequent API calls. Scope limited to CLI initialization.

eli5.text: When you start up the assistant, it now quietly checks whether your paid subscription is still valid, so any changes to your account (like an expired or renewed plan) are picked up right away instead of being discovered mid-conversation. This only happens if you've already signed in with your account at startup, and if the check fails for any reason, it won't stop you; the assistant will just try again later. It's live today for anyone launching the assistant from the command line.

ai.title: Track Claude OAuth analytics events in SDK
ai.summary: Added `CLAUDE_OAUTH_REQUEST`, `CLAUDE_OAUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, and `CLAUDE_OAUTH_AUTH_ERROR` to `AnalyticsEvent` enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. `promptAiSdkStream` in `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` now calls `trackEvent` for these states, passing `userId`, `model`, and `userInputId`. Scope limited to SDK and shared core constants. Event tracking now precedes the `onClaudeOAuthStatusChange` callback.

eli5.text: When you connect to Claude through the SDK using OAuth, the system now sends anonymous usage events to track when a request is made, when you get rate limited, and when there is an authentication error. If you looked at your analytics dashboard, you'd see new event types like 'claude_oauth_request' and 'claude_oauth_auth_error' recorded with your model and input ID but without exposing any sensitive token data.

ai.title: Add note to CLI out-of-credits banner
ai.summary: Adds a note to the CLI out-of-credits banner stating that some credits are needed even with a Claude subscription for other model usage. This clarifies that a subscription does not cover all model usage. The change is in `cli/src/components/out-of-credits-banner.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you run out of credits, you now see an extra line on the message that tells you a paid subscription does not cover every model you can pick, so you still need some credits for those. The note appears only on that out-of-credits screen before you buy more, and nothing else about the message changed.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version 1.0.575 ships OAuth refresh, GPT-5 reviewer
ai.summary: This release bundles a version bump to 1.0.575 in cli/release/package.json, alongside several functional improvements shipping across the CLI, SDK, and agent packages. Notable changes include automatic refresh of Claude OAuth credentials on CLI startup via initializeApp in cli/src/init/init-app.ts, a new reviewer-editor-gpt-5 agent replacing code-reviewer in max mode for high-reasoning reviews, and the base2 validation prompt now skipping typechecks for changes under 10 lines to reduce overhead. Minor improvements include labeled beta status for /ads:enable and /ads:disable commands, tracked Claude OAuth analytics events in the SDK, a reduced ad payload sending only the last three user messages, clarified out-of-credits messaging, and preserved web researcher subagent output in the CLI via spawn ID-based block matching.
ai.evidence: Commit 8d6eb2e0 modifies cli/release/package.json, changing the "version" field from "1.0.574" to "1.0.575". No functional code changes are present in the diff, consistent with the commit nature being a release-bump with a single +1/-1 line modification. Contextual evidence from the same-day commit sequence confirms this is part of the 1.0.575 release cycle, with the actual user-visible changes described in the attached release notes.

eli5.text: This release upgrades the Freebuff CLI to version 1.0.575 with a smarter AI code reviewer powered by GPT-5, improved OAuth login stability, and fixes for displaying subagent output in your terminal. The main highlight is a new GPT-5-based reviewer that activates in "max mode" to provide deeper, higher-quality code review feedback for larger or more complex changes. The CLI now refreshes your Claude OAuth credentials automatically when you start it up, so your subscription status stays current without manual logins. Web researcher subagent output now displays correctly in the terminal, fixing a previous bug where streamed content could be lost or misattributed. The out-of-credits warning banner now clarifies that a Claude subscription does not cover all model usage, helping you understand when you may still need credits. Upgrading gives you more reliable authentication, clearer error messaging, and a more capable AI reviewer for your most demanding coding tasks.

ai.title: Claude Connect Banner Auto-Opens OAuth Browser
ai.summary: ClaudeConnectBanner now auto-triggers openOAuthInBrowser on mount when getClaudeOAuthStatus returns disconnected. This replaces the static 'not-connected' state with an immediate 'waiting-for-code' flow. Error handling catches browser launch failures and transitions to 'error' state. Change applies to cli/src/components/claude-connect-banner.tsx.

eli5.text: When you try to sign in to Claude through the command-line tool and you're not already signed in, the app now automatically opens your web browser to the sign-in page instead of just showing a message asking you to do it manually. Once the browser window appears, you complete the sign-in on the web, and if the browser can't open for some reason, you'll see an error message telling you what went wrong. This change is already live and affects anyone who tries to connect using the command-line version of Claude.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.576 release bump
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.576 in cli/release/package.json, packaging the same-day release. This release adds automatic OAuth browser launch from the Claude Connect banner when disconnected, refresh of Claude OAuth credentials during CLI initialization, a GPT-5 high-reasoning reviewer-agent-gpt-5 agent replacing code-reviewer in max mode, and a base2 validation prompt that skips typechecking for changes under 10 lines. The slash command list was reordered to prioritize connect:claude and init, and /ads:enable and /ads:disable are now labeled beta.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version bumped from 1.0.575 to 1.0.576 (single-line diff). Surrounding same-day release work included Claude Connect banner auto-opening OAuth browser on disconnect, refresh of Claude OAuth credentials on CLI init, reviewer-editor-gpt-5 agent in max mode, and base2 validation skipping typecheck for changes under 10 lines.

eli5.text: This release streamlines how you connect your Freebuff CLI to Claude, so linking your account is faster and requires less manual effort. When the on-screen connection banner appears and it detects that you aren't yet linked, it now immediately opens your web browser to the login page, taking you straight to the authorization step instead of leaving you to click through a static message. If something goes wrong and the browser can't launch, the banner clearly shows an error rather than hanging silently. Upgrading gives you a smoother, more reliable setup flow for connecting Claude, so you spend less time troubleshooting authentication and more time building. Overall, the connection step just works the way you'd expect it to from any modern app.

ai.title: Reorder CLI slash command list and help banner shortcuts
ai.summary: Reordered SLASH_COMMANDS array in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts to prioritize connect:claude and init, moving ads:enable, ads:disable, referral, and logout/exit to the end. Updated help-banner.tsx to display /commands first in the shortcut list. Removed commented-out undo, redo, and checkpoint entries. No functional changes to command logic.

eli5.text: You'll now see /connect:claude and /init at the top of the slash-command list in the CLI's help screen, with commands like logout, exit, and beta ad toggles moved to the bottom; the help banner also now leads with '/commands' as its first shortcut. This is a live visual reorder only, no command behavior changed, nothing new can do yet, and the older undo/redo/checkpoint entries were removed since they were never active.
